I don't know of an environment variable that sets a pass-rate threshold for `promptfoo eval`. The retrieved docs don't name one.

The docs show pass-rate gates implemented in the CI shell script, with the 95% threshold hardcoded: "if (( $(echo "$PASS_RATE < 95" | bc -l) )); then" [promptfoo/site/docs/integrations/ci-cd.md]. The docs also describe a separate flag: "# Fail on any test failures" [promptfoo/site/docs/integrations/ci-cd.md], which corresponds to `--fail-on-error`. That flag fails on errors rather than on a configurable pass rate. The AWS CodeCommit page says a custom threshold is an alternative to that flag: "If you want a custom pass-rate threshold instead of `--fail-on-error`, write the JSON output and check the stats in a second command:" [promptfoo/site/docs/integrations/aws-codecommit.md].

The environment variable reference in `promptfoo/site/docs/usage/command-line.md` is cut off in the retrieved context, so I can't rule out a variable listed there. Checking the full table or the `promptfoo eval` options in that file would settle it.
